title: Registry and archive downloads refuse URLs that are not credential-free HTTPS
summary: `fetchBounded` (`@inventarch/distribution/internal/bounded-fetch`), the one request behind registry documents and remote archives, now checks the URL itself before any request, even when its caller did not. It parses the URL with `new URL` and refuses only a URL that does not parse, whose scheme is not `https:` or that has a username or password, with `IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID` naming the URL. It then requests the canonical form `new URL` writes, so a legitimate non-canonical HTTPS spelling, such as an uppercase host, an explicit `:443`, a percent-encoded host character, a query or a fragment, is canonicalized and still accepted, and fetch makes the same request as before: a direct caller, or a hand-built `RegistryBase`, that passes an HTTPS URL sees no break. A malformed or credentialed URL got no request before either (fetch rejected it, reported as `IA-DIST-ARTIFACT-UNAVAILABLE`); a URL with another scheme, which could be fetched before (`http:` in clear text, a `data:` URL), now refuses. URLs built on a `parseRegistryBase` base and URLs the archive check admits are already canonical and are requested unchanged. Migration: direct callers can keep passing URLs, or use `parseRegistryBase` to get the canonical form up front. This is URL-shape hygiene, not host authorization: it does not block internal or loopback hosts, DNS rebinding or other server-side request forgery. Redirects, the 30-second timeout and the byte bounds are unchanged.
